scenes.headline: How LongCat 2.0's sparse attention reads less of the past
scenes.sub: Meituan's open MoE, and the three moves inside LongCat Sparse Attention
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nougat! LongCat 2.0 is Meituan's open mixture of experts, with about forty-eight billion parameters active per token. Here's how its attention reads less.

scenes.text: Score the past cheaply, then read only a token-precise slice of it: candidate blocks first, then the best tokens inside them.
scenes.say: The idea: score the past cheaply, then read only a token-precise slice of it. Candidate blocks first, then the best tokens inside them.

steps.label: Full attention: every past token
steps.say: Under full attention, every query reads every past token. Over a long context, that is brutal to serve.

steps.label: Coarse recall: candidate blocks
steps.say: Hierarchical indexing starts coarse. A cheap block-level pass proposes candidate blocks, the way MiniMax's sparse attention keeps whole blocks.

steps.label: Fine pass: single tokens
steps.say: Then a fine pass selects the most relevant individual tokens inside them. Token-precise, over a smaller set the indexer has to score.

scenes.title: Three cuts to the indexer's cost
scenes.say: Its sparse attention attacks the indexer from three sides.

items.say: Hierarchical indexing shrinks what the indexer has to score.
Cross-layer indexing shares one index every two layers, since saliency is stable between neighbours. Half the layers reuse a selection instead of recomputing it.
Streaming-aware indexing mixes contiguous reads with random picks, so the reads it does issue are cheaper.
One honest note: the public SGLang path drops the hierarchical stage, so what ships today is the other two.

left.title: Add more experts
items: Past MoE's sweet spot, N-grams beat it
left.say: The usual way to add capacity is more experts. Meituan says that past a sweet spot in sparsity, an n-gram embedding wins instead.

right.title: Add an N-gram embedding
items: 135B parameters in a token n-gram lookup
Sparse, and orthogonal to the MoE
right.say: So LongCat also carries a hundred and thirty-five billion parameters in an n-gram embedding: a lookup, orthogonal to the experts.

scenes.text: Each move targets a distinct cost: what the indexer scores, how often it runs, and how cheaply it reads.

recap: Coarse blocks first, then token-precise picks
One index shared across every 2 layers
A 135B n-gram lookup beside the experts
scenes.say: To recap: blocks then tokens, one index per two layers, and an n-gram lookup beside the experts.
